# Compacted Summary: Chapters 1-18 (Extended v138)

## Setting and Time
Multiple periods spanning French Revolution to 1826. **Current narrative point (October 1831, early morning, Barrière du Maine)**: Paris—Gorbeau house (50-52, Salpêtrière district); Rue de la Verrerie (Courfeyrac's residence); Rue Plumet (Valjean's primary house); Rue de Babylone (secret passage exit); Rue de l'Homme Armé (secondary apartment); Rue de l'Ouest (secondary apartment); Luxembourg; Saint-Jacques-du-Haut-Pas church; Barrière du Maine; Rue de Sèvres; inner boulevard; Dunstead (harbor town in English provinces); Staveford; Wilwick (hill farms—Luena Stenenridge, Rozek Stenenridge); Rovus Prydenridge's location. **Environmental details**: Frost silvered hedges; chalked crooked sun on forge wall; rain threatened; wind carries salt/tar scent; road ruts and puddles after thaw; light goes early; smoke lies flat; bells ring for vespers; baker's boy often late; lines at oven grow long; cart loaded with turnips creaks past well; children chase hoop shrieking; dogs bark at nothing; gulls quarrel over fish heads by steps; chimneys smoke flat over fields; bees hum in lavender behind parsonage. October 1831 dawn: few constellations in pale azure, earth black, heavens white, mysterious chill of twilight, lark carolling at height, Venus rising brilliantly behind Val-de-Grâce dome.

## Primary Locations
**RUE PLUMET HOUSE**: Single-story pavilion in deserted Rue Plumet with garden approximately one-and-a-half acres. Two ground-floor rooms, two first-floor chambers, downstairs kitchen, upstairs boudoir, attic. Behind pavilion: narrow courtyard, low building (two rooms, cellar). Secret-spring door masked in building communicates via long narrow paved winding corridor to Rue de Babylone quarter-league distant. Originally built mid-last-century by Paris Parliament chief justice as mistress-house; October 1829: Valjean hired and repaired as M. Fauchelevent. **Garden characteristics**: Left uncultivated; silvery snail tracks on cold yellow leaf carpet in winter; breathes melancholy, solitude, liberty, absence of man, presence of God; ancient padlocked gate twisted, tottering; former coquettish garden now magnificent disheveled obscurity; nature filled with shade arranged for love. **Access strategy**: Valjean, Cosette, Toussaint enter/emerge only via Rue de Babylone door.

**POOR MEADOWS NEAR BARRIÈRE DU MAINE (October 1831)**: Nearly confounded with city; grow sickly grain in summer; after autumn harvest appear peeled rather than reaped. Solitary, beloved by Valjean for freedom and privacy it offers Cosette.

## Jean Valjean's Crisis and Altered Routine (April Year 4 through October 1831)
**The ambush aftermath**: M. Leblanc (Cosette's biological father) escaped unscrewing coin piece and cutting cords; Javert positioned outside, captured Thénardier and gang. Valjean subsequently relocated with Cosette to Rue Plumet (October 1829) as M. Fauchelevent.

**Valjean and Marius conflict (Spring-Summer Year 5)**: Marius initially indifferent toward Cosette, then began paying attention (wearing new coat daily, uncertain if hair curled, wearing gloves, exhibiting awkward unnatural behavior). Valjean detected these changes through old Mother Nature's warning. Marius attempted to keep out of sight but Valjean occasionally espied him. Valjean instituted undeclared war: changed hours, changed benches, forgot handkerchief, came alone to Luxembourg, laid ambushes. Marius dashed headlong into all snares. Cosette remained immured in apparent unconcern, so Valjean concluded "that ninny is madly in love with Cosette, but Cosette does not even know that he exists." Valjean cordially detested Marius; experienced moments when thought becoming savage and ferocious, felt old depths of soul formerly containing wrath opening once more.

**Marius's pursuit and Valjean's withdrawal (Summer Year 5)**: Marius followed Cosette to Rue de l'Ouest. Spoke to porter. Porter reported to Valjean: "Monsieur, who is that curious young man who is asking for you?" **One week later, Valjean bestowed on Marius that glance which Marius at last perceived.** Valjean swore to himself never again to set foot in Luxembourg or Rue de l'Ouest. **Returned permanently to Rue Plumet.**

**Valjean's anguish over Cosette's transformation**: Recognizes Cosette escaping from him. Suffers greatly, becomes puerile; unconquerable conviction that Cosette is slipping away. Wishes to resist, retain her, arouse her enthusiasm by external brilliant matter. Once saw General Comte Coutard on horseback in full uniform; envied gilded man, fantasized putting on uniform so Cosette would be dazzled and fixed in her devotion to him. Contemplates cloister—that chaste peak, inaccessible glacier of virtue—with despairing ecstasy; regrets his abnegation in bringing Cosette back into world. Passes whole nights on pallet with head in hands asking "What has Cosette in her mind?" and "What is taking place in Cosette's soul?" Experiences grave significance of her silence: she says nothing, asks no questions, seeks not his reasons, already afraid of being divined and betraying herself.

## Cosette's Coming of Age and Hidden Love (Summer Year 5—October 1831)
**Physical transformation complete**: Beautiful for tolerably long time before aware; consciousness of beauty burst upon her like sudden daylight. Skin white, hair lustrous, blue eyes gained unaccustomed splendor. Lost grace of ignoring beauty; gained pensive serious charm. Whole person permeated with joy of youth; innocence and beauty breathed forth splendid melancholy.

**Coquetry awakened and appearance changed**: Conceived horror for merinos, shame for plush hat. Father never refused anything. Acquired whole science of bonnet, gown, mantle, boot, cuff, stuff in fashion. First outing in new attire: black damask gown, white crape bonnet, gay, radiant, rosy, proud, dazzling. Valjean replied "Charming!" in voice resembling bitter envious man.

**Love for Marius (Excerpt 1094-1099)**: Two souls prepared—Cosette in her shadow, Marius in his, charged and languishing with stormy electricity of passion. **When their eyes met at last**, Cosette did not immediately understand. Returned thoughtfully to Rue de l'Ouest house. **Next morning**: Thought of strange young man now paying attention to her. Not least bit agreeable; incensed at handsome disdainful individual. Substratum of war stirred within her; struck her with wholly childish joy: would take revenge. Assessed him: beautiful hair, eyes, teeth, charming tone, held himself badly walking but with grace, seemed not stupid, noble, gentle, simple, proud, though poor, air fine.

**First initiative (Excerpt 1096)**: Remained on bench; vexed Cosette. One day said to Valjean: "Father, let us stroll about a little in that direction." When Marius did not come to her, she went to him. In such cases, all women resemble Mahomet; first symptom of true love in young man is timidity, in young girl is boldness.

**Passionate ignorance (Excerpt 1097-1099)**: First felt confused profound melancholy; soul seemed blackened. Did not know what love was; never heard word in terrestrial sense. **Loved with all passion because loved ignorantly.** Did not know whether good/bad, useful/dangerous, eternal/temporary, allowable/prohibited; loved. Would have been astonished by reproach for not sleeping, not eating, heart palpitations, blushing/paling. Loved ignorantly, without name, fault, spot, exigence, defect. He was not lover, not even admirer—vision. Set herself to adoring Marius as charming, luminous, impossible. Distant lover lingering in ideal, chimæra with form. Any nearer meeting would have alarmed her, still half immersed in convent's exaggerated mists. Had all fears of children and nuns combined; convent spirit still slowly evaporating.

**Silence and concealment (after October 1831 withdrawal)**: Cosette did not complain, said nothing, asked no questions, sought not Valjean's reasons. Already reached point where afraid of being divined, of betraying herself. Valjean had no experience of these miseries—the only charming miseries, only ones he did not know; consequently did not understand grave significance of Cosette's silence.

**October 1831 matutinal excursions**: Rise early before daybreak; trips planned on preceding evening—he proposed, she agreed, arranged like plot. Innocent eccentricities pleasing to young people. Matutinal walks equivalent to night stroll with added cheerfulness of nature; streets deserted, birds singing. Cosette a bird herself, liked to rise early. Loved these excursions.

**Poor meadows behavior**: Valjean loved haunt these fields for solitude; liberty they offered Cosette. She became little girl once more, ran and almost played. Took off hat, laid it on Valjean's knees, gathered bunches of flowers. Gazed at butterflies on flowers but did not catch them; gentleness and tenderness born with love—young girl cherishing fragile ideal has mercy on butterfly wing. Wove garlands of poppies, placed on head, crossed and penetrated with sunlight, glowing until they flamed, formed for rosy face crown of burning embers.

## Marius Pontmercy: Psychological and Financial Crisis
**Identity**: Baron Marius Pontmercy, twenty years old; three years estranged from grandfather. Paternal legacy: Colonel's instruction regarding Waterloo sergeant Thénardier.

**Financial crisis (Spring-Summer Year 5)**: **First time in life, borrowed five francs from Courfeyrac; now borrows hundred-sou piece (five francs).** Poverty returned; felt icy breath. Old coat impossible; new coat growing old; shirts, hat, boots wearing out. Cannot focus on work—turning celebrated German quarrel into French. Cannot focus: reads four lines, attempts to write one, sees star between himself and paper, abandons task.

**Psychological state**: Passion precipitated him into chimæras without object or bottom. Lost faculty of working toward fixed goal but endowed with more clear-sightedness and rectitude than ever. Judgment almost wholly disassociated from hope. Meditation turns to reproach; reflects dolefully on idleness, paralysis of soul gaining on him, night growing more dense. No longer even sees sun. Yet sensations reach him: laundresses beating linen, birds chattering in elm-trees. Happy, even in anguish.

**Change in demeanor and secret**: Once long indifferent and icy toward Cosette, now pays attention; wears new coat daily, uncertain whether has hair curled, wears gloves, exhibits awkward unnatural behavior—all observed and detested by Valjean. **Periodical five francs a double riddle**: to Courfeyrac who lent, to unknown recipient (Cosette) who received.

## Éponine's Reconnaissance (Year 5)
**Status**: Released from Les Madelonettes. Magnon handed Brujon's note. Went to Rue Plumet, recognized gate and garden, observed house, spied, lurked. Brought biscuit (prison symbol) to Magnon, transmitted to Babet's mistress. Network spreading, prison communication via "postilion"—moulded bread pallet sent rooftop courtyard-to-courtyard with notes.

## October 1831 Morning—Barrière du Maine (Excerpt 1110-1112)
**Scene**: October morning, tempted by serene perfection of autumn 1831, Valjean and Cosette set out, found themselves at break of day near Barrière du Maine. Not dawn, but daybreak—delightful, stern moment. Few constellations in deep pale azure, earth black, heavens white, quiver amid blades of grass, mysterious chill of twilight. Lark mingled with stars, carolling at prodigious height, hymn of pettiness calming immensity. In East, Val-de-Grâce projected dark mass on clear horizon with sharpness of steel; Venus dazzlingly brilliant rising behind dome, air of soul escaping gloomy edifice.

**Valjean's profound absorption**: Sitting in cross-walk on planks at timber-yard gate, face toward highway, back toward light. Forgotten sun on point of rising. Sunk into profound absorption—meditation called vertical. Thinking of Cosette, happiness possible if nothing came between them, light with which she filled his life, emanation of her soul. Almost happy in reverie. Cosette standing beside him, gazing at clouds turning rosy.

**Approaching event (Excerpt 1112)**: Causeway leading to ancient Barrière du Maine prolongation of Rue de Sèvres, cut at right angles by inner boulevard. At elbow of causeway and boulevard, at spot where branches, heard noise difficult to account for at that hour. Sort of confused pile made appearance. Some shapeless thing coming from boulevard turning into road.
